(1) The sentence as written is false: a dependent of lower need can arise for ever below its renewers' need (countermodel). For dependents at a need of at least m it is already Flow.ends_below with "active" weakened to "arises". What is new is short: below the gate nothing is given again, so arising that takes does not recur. (2) The kernel statement is true, about 12 lines, and is ends_iff_below with both sides negated: a renaming. (3) ends_iff_below is not a case of leading_exact and is not derived so. The join that exists is threshold_regime, which runs from the regime to the plane; its premise that giving rises looks droppable.

seat:cancer-and-the-line.answer_in_one_paragraph: AI-written (Fable), 16 November 2026. Neither link holds as a theorem. (1) Apart, both ways. `ConfinedRise.ends` is a lineage ending with a whole whose conditions fall below their gate and do not return. `line_ends` is a line ending alone, below its own need, on a stock that can recover while other units go on (C). The Web-with-a-Flow dictionary is an obstacle here too (a flow and a web must be defined from the course), but it is not why they are apart: C balances at every step. What decides whether the line takes the whole with it is the order of needs: where the line has one need and every other unit needs at least that, the net ends when the line does (argued by hand, one side only; 1,500 random worlds, none against). (2) The ending laws are not cases of each other; the counting under them is proved twice. The rise is one definition: `generations_rise` is `MoreThanNow` unfolded, so `need_unmet` derives the step-by-step rise, from `grows`, which stays supplied. It is not derived from what taking gains: a unit's kids do not depend on its use.

links.statement: A closed line whose kids of the line take more is a `ConfinedRise` on the stock, its excess derived.
links.evidence: Founding.lean:161-175; LineOnAStock.lean:904-911. Under `ends`' base premises, with one condition whose level is the course's: `excess` and balance make the level fall throughout [T, T+n); afterwards `family_excess_ends` (Continuation.lean:573) with `gated` and `acting` leaves nothing given; `draws` puts T at or before the line's last step. So the level never rises from T on. In C it does.

Why nothing returns differs: there the gate keeps the conditions down; here the level may return and `closed` leaves no unit to restart.
